claim_boundary.promotion_rule: Reopen and verify a source, then promote only a narrow claim into KREATE/EVIDENCE.md when path ownership allows.

primary_sources.title: Boğaziçi University Greenhouse Gas Inventory Report 2025

facts.label: PUBLIC_SOURCE
facts.claim: Boğaziçi reports 48,251 kg total food waste in 2025.
facts.caveat: Does not establish avoidability, causal mechanism or forecast error.

facts.label: PUBLIC_SOURCE
facts.claim: The university states that it provides catering to approximately 13,000 students and 2,000 staff and lists six dining halls with 1,734 total listed capacity.
facts.caveat: Nominal community size and dining-hall capacity are not meal attendance counts.

facts.label: PUBLIC_SOURCE
facts.claim: An official food-service page states that meals served by dining halls are prepared in the North Campus kitchen, with backup kitchens for technical failure/disaster.
facts.caveat: Centralized preparation does not identify the production-quantity decision owner, buyer or approval timing.

facts.label: PUBLIC_SOURCE
facts.claim: Boğaziçi publicly describes existing food-waste actions including portion control, removal of unpopular dishes, composting, surplus handling/donation and recycling.
facts.caveat: The public sources do not quantify the marginal effectiveness of each action.

facts.label: DERIVED_PUBLIC_SERIES_STATISTIC
facts.claim: Published 2025 monthly food-waste totals range from 1,334 kg to 7,811 kg; max/min is approximately 5.86 and coefficient of variation approximately 52.6%.
facts.caveat: Variation does not prove unpredictable demand; calendar, service days, occupancy, menu mix or accounting timing may explain it.

facts.label: SOURCE_DATA_QUALITY_FLAG
facts.claim: The food-waste table contains months where reported amount delivered to İSTAÇ exceeds the same month's total food waste despite a note that delivered amounts are included in totals.
facts.caveat: August is 1,502 kg total vs 3,550 kg delivered; October is 1,334 kg total vs 4,850 kg delivered. Do not infer the cause.

facts.label: PUBLIC_SOURCE
facts.claim: Menus are announced ahead of service, food engineers prepare menus, and nutritional/portion information is specified or published.
facts.caveat: Public documentation does not prove historical row-level data are accessible for modeling.

facts.label: PUBLIC_SOURCE
facts.claim: Boğaziçi publicly documents grey-water and rainwater recovery and states that grey water supplies 15% of total water consumption in the 1st Men's Dormitory.
facts.caveat: The same page contains differing descriptions of the 16 m3/day figure, so that number needs clarification before submission use.

facts.label: PUBLIC_SOURCE
facts.claim: The 2025 sustainable-practices table reports 65 personnel shuttles, 7 campus shuttle services, capacity 1,429, occupancy 93%, and 1,332 users.
facts.caveat: These figures do not by themselves establish a mobility pain point or optimization gap.

facts.label: PUBLIC_SOURCE
facts.claim: The 2025 GHG inventory reports total emissions of 14,664.76 tCO2e, with 45.61% electricity, 34.73% natural gas, 3.57% stationary/mobile combustion and 16.09% Scope 3/value-chain emissions.
facts.caveat: Corporate inventory context; it does not allocate a food-waste intervention impact.

derived_food_waste_statistics.interpretation_limit: Descriptive only; do not treat as forecast-error evidence.

critical_unknowns_for_pmr: When is the production quantity frozen or hard to change?
If reservations exist, what is the no-show behavior?
What share of waste is preparation, unserved surplus, serving loss, or post-consumer plate waste?
What happens operationally when demand exceeds production?
What is the relative penalty of shortage versus excess?
Are planned, produced, served and discarded quantities recorded at campus-meal granularity?
Can operators cook in multiple batches or change quantities during service?
Why do August and October İSTAÇ delivery figures exceed same-month total food-waste figures?

IE: Interview Food Services/HKS operations, central-kitchen contractor/manager, food engineers, campus service managers and waste/procurement owners.
Test decision timing/discretion, demand-mismatch causality and real decision authority using last-incident questions.
Do not turn 48,251 kg into a causal forecasting claim.
EE: Map planned portions -> produced/batches -> served -> unserved surplus -> preparation/plate waste -> destination.
Record unit, timestamp, campus, meal, owner, burden and auditability for each measurement.
Prefer existing logs and manual weighing/counts before proposing new hardware.
CS1: Start with simple campus-meal-calendar baselines before complex ML.
Use asymmetric waste/shortage loss and explicit abstention/override semantics.
Do not use the monthly public waste table as training data without a reconciled data dictionary and finer-grained operational data.
Benchmark reservation/show-no-show features only if PMR confirms they exist.
CS2: Frame the 48,251 kg total and existing mitigation as PUBLIC SOURCE context.
Keep the remaining production-mismatch opportunity explicitly HYPOTHESIS until PMR validates it.
Never claim the literature's reported reductions as expected or achieved Boğaziçi impact.
